newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria wants border committee for oil-rich seas.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria wants border committee for oil-rich seas.

text.p: Nigeria has called for a commission to mark out boundaries in Africa's oil-rich Gulf of Guinea and avoid wars between neighbouring countries.
Lieutenant-General Oladipo Diya, number two in Nigeria's military leadership, said the commission should include Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon and Sao Tome and Principe as well as Nigeria.

He was speaking at a meeting of officials from Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea in the capital on Wednesday to discuss their maritime border which runs through the Zafiro oil field where Mobil began production from Equatorial Guinea in 1995.

Nigeria's border dispute with Cameroon over the Bakassi peninsula, which may hold significant oil reserves, has flared into fighting times since 1992 and the two armies sit eyeball to eyeball across the swampy creeks.
Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, pumps far more oil than its neighbours and production stands at around two million barrels of crude per day.
